question_text:
The invention of the X is a classic example of "legal engineering" - where a business owner created a new product specifically to bypass a strict religious law.
In the late 19th century, many American towns (particularly in the Midwest) enforced Blue Laws. These were religious statutes designed to keep the Sabbath holy by banning "frisky" or sinful activities on Sundays.
At the time, Y were the most popular treat in the country. However, religious leaders in places like Evanston, Illinois, and various towns in Wisconsin considered the fizzy nature of the treat to be too indulgent for a Sunday. Consequently, many municipalities passed laws banning the sale of the fizzy ingredient on the Lord's Day.
Local druggists and confectioners, facing a huge loss in Sunday revenue, had to get creative. Around 1881, a shop owner (most famously attributed to Edward Berners) decided to serve the Y without the fizzy ingredient, paving way for X. Id X (5), Y (5).
answer_text: X = Ice Cream Sundae; Y = Ice Cream Soda

The story of Ernest Vincent Wright and his 1939 novel Gadsby is one of the most extreme examples of a "constrained writing" challenge ever attempted. The motivation came from a bet. Wright was a 66-year-old Navy veteran who wrote the book primarily to settle a recurring argument. People told him it was impossible to write a long-form story with a constraint. To prove them wrong, he spent 165 days (about five and a half months) writing the 50,110-word manuscript. One paragraph reads:
"Upon this basis I am going to try a long story. It is a story about a small town. It is not a story about a big city. It is a story about a group of boys and girls."
What is the constraint?
answer_text: The novel doesn't contain the letter 'E' anywhere in its text

Artist Salvatore Garau, who made international headlines in May 2021 when he sold a sculpture Io Sono (which translates to "I Am") for EUR15,000 (approx. $18,300). The sculpture came with a certificate of authentication and specific instructions for its installation:
The sculpture had to be housed in a private home within a space measuring roughly 5x5 feet (150x150 cm).
The area had to be free from any obstructions but had no instructions on the lighting and climate control.
Later another artist named Tom Miller claimed he had already created this sculpture in 2016 and threatened to sue Garau for "plagiarism of his idea," though legal experts struggled to define how one proves the "theft" of this idea. What was the idea?

In 1946, X was a professor at the University of Chicago but based in Wisconsin. When he was assigned to teach an advanced astrophysics course, only two students - T.D. Lee and C.N. Yang - registered for it. Despite the tiny enrollment and the brutal winter weather, X refused to cancel the class. Twice a week, he drove a 160-mile round trip in the snow just to deliver his lectures, driven by a deep sense of duty and the recognition that his two pupils possessed extraordinary potential.
Just a decade later, in 1957, both Lee and Yang were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for their work on parity laws. The story came full circle in 1983 when X himself was awarded the Nobel Prize, meaning that every single person in that small classroom - the teacher and both students - eventually became a Nobel Laureate. Id X.

The Indo-Bangladesh enclaves, known as X, were a collection of 162 land fragments that created one of the world's most baffling border anomalies for nearly 70 years. According to local legend, these pockets of territory were the result of high-stakes chess games (1713) between the Maharaja of Y and the Mughal Faujdar of Rangpur, who allegedly staked entire villages on their matches. This resulted in a fragmented map where pieces of India were marooned inside Bangladesh and vice-versa, including the world's only third-order enclave - a patch of India sitting inside a Bangladeshi patch, which was itself inside an Indian patch, all surrounded by Bangladesh.
This historical headache finally ended on August 1, 2015, when India and Bangladesh executed a historic Land Boundary Agreement. The two nations swapped the enclaves and allowed thousands of residents to finally choose their nationality and gain the citizenship rights they had been denied for decades. Id X (5) and Y (5).
answer_text: X = Chitmahals / Pasha Enclaves; Y = Cooch Behar
